name: Person-First Education Workspace
intent: A calm person-first education surface. The learner's current evidenced relation determines movement; academic visual grammar supplies stable orientation through subject identity, current work, upcoming movement, recent feedback/evidence, and resumable learning without turning grades, scores, schedules, or course sequence into learner truth.

reference_policy.use: External schools and learning platforms are visual/interaction witnesses only. Swallow useful relations; do not inherit their product model.
forbid: institutional workflow copied merely because a witness uses it

witnesses.notes: Internal witness produced from the education-kernel architecture. Preserve learner-first hierarchy and separation of present relation from obligations.
Reference only, not a copy contract. K12 witness: familiar learner navigation keeps schedules, classes, announcements, resources and current school activity easy to reach.
Reference only, not a copy contract. Acellus witness: current classes and immediate return to the student's current position make re-entry obvious.
Reference only, not a copy contract. Time4Learning witness: learners can enter through current courses/activity cards and parents can keep planning/reporting deeper in their own view.
Reference only, not a copy contract. Outschool witness: learner space and parent space are distinct; the learner view keeps schedule, class entry and learner tools close to the person.
Reference only, not a copy contract. Homeschool Planet witness: color can provide quick person/subject orientation and schedule tools can remain useful without owning the learning model.
Canvas witness: dashboard as landing orientation; course identity, agenda/to-do, recent activity, upcoming work and feedback are separate but globally reachable.
Moodle witness: activity overview preserves activity type, dates, completion requirements, submission state and course context without requiring navigation through every course section.
Moodle witness: dashboard is treated as a central starting point with quick access to courses; simplified subsection presentation reduces bordered-box fragmentation.
Blackboard witness: persistent academic orientation through courses, calendar, activity stream, messages and grades; activity stream answers what requires attention now.
edX witness: current courses and a direct View Course/continue action provide a simple learner entry into ongoing work.
Khan witness: teacher-side progress and student skill detail are useful deeper views, but progress metrics must remain subordinate to actual evidence in this system.

layout.shape: learner → subject/course orientation → in front now / continue → today and upcoming → recent feedback/evidence → deeper map and operator layers
layout.grouping: current learner truth, academic orientation, obligations, artifacts, feedback/evidence, and operating schedule remain visually distinct
layout.primary_action: continue the next supported educational movement
layout.secondary_actions: record observation, open learning details, inspect evidence, create artifact, or adjust local activity

academic_orientation.subject_identity: stable visual anchor; use subject/course labels to orient without making subject the kernel
academic_orientation.current_work: one obvious resumable movement should dominate the learner-facing hierarchy
academic_orientation.upcoming: dates and due/upcoming relations orient time but do not define the learning path
academic_orientation.recent_feedback: surface returned work/evidence near current movement; avoid hiding feedback in a separate administrative area
academic_orientation.progress: use descriptive evidence/state and movement history; percentage/mastery displays may orient only when their witness is explicit and must not stand in for learner truth
academic_orientation.navigation: courses/subjects, calendar/today, activity/evidence and materials should remain predictable across sessions
academic_orientation.density: prefer academic scanability: headings/dividers/lists before card-per-field fragmentation

controls.treatment: conventional academic controls with plain labels
controls.advanced_options: kept outside the learner's current movement unless reached

surface.cards: course/subject or meaningful state boundaries only; use headers and dividers for subordinate structure
surface.color: neutral base with restrained subject accents and one functional primary accent

typography.tone: plain, precise, academically legible, not institutional or childish
typography.hierarchy: learner/current movement scans before administrative metrics or standards

motion.rule: state changes after evidence/activity return; no decorative motion

avoid: conventional LMS gradebook as the primary surface
institutional navigation for its own sake
streaks, points, badges, or guilt language
grade level presented as learner truth
schedule or course sequence presented as the learner path
percentage progress used as a substitute for evidence
adaptation_rules: Translate kernel language into ordinary academic learner language on the default surface; keep precise kernel terminology in deeper/operator views.
Give every active movement a stable subject/course identity when one exists.
Make one current supported movement resumable through an obvious Continue/Start action.
Keep Today/Upcoming and recent feedback/evidence close to the current movement.
Current learner relations must remain upstream of curriculum obligations even when obligations are displayed through familiar course/subject navigation.
Grade context may appear only as obligation/reporting context.
Manual observation entry should be secondary to normal learning movement and returned evidence.
Artifacts must retain provenance and be treated as evidence surfaces, not mastery claims.
Prefer section headings and dividers over many equally weighted cards.
Keep the operator surface academically familiar without importing institutional bureaucracy that has no current relation.

review.notes: Expanded with academic visual witnesses from Canvas, Moodle, Blackboard, edX and Khan Academy. Academic grammar is used for orientation only; learner truth remains evidence-grounded.
